    Key words The key words MUST, MUST NOT, SHOULD, SHOULD NOT and MAY in this chapter are to be interpreted as described in RFC 2119.

    §5.1 What the stack supports

    The policy lists the MySQL versions in policy/policy.json, under mysql: 5.6, 5.7, 8.0, 8.4 and 9.7, each with its active_until and security_until dates. The shared server runs 5.6, which is past security support; its security_until is 2021-02-28. Laravel 13 documents MySQL 5.7 or later, and each Laravel line in the policy records the oldest MySQL and MariaDB it needs (requires.mysql and requires.mariadb); PROCTOR 0.10.0's mysql-minimum warns when an app's declared database image is below that minimum. The conventions below keep an app working on the shared server until it is upgraded. They are a bridge, not the fix: the fix is the upgrade. Code that follows them runs unchanged on 8.4, so the move can be made With Arms Wide Open.

    §5.2 Which MySQL lines the policy lists

    The policy lists the LTS lines, 8.4 and 9.7, for current use. It keeps the older lines, 5.6, 5.7 and 8.0, only to say that they are end of life. In MySQL 8.4 and later the default authentication plugin is caching_sha2_password: mysql_native_password is disabled by default in 8.4 and removed in 9.0. An app that MUST reach a server on the older plugin MUST set the server's plugin explicitly in its database config. No check exists yet.

    §5.3 Grace period

    An app MAY stay on a database version for 90 days after it leaves support, the policy's eol_grace_days; the version is Eol through that window and EolGraceExpired the day after. The window is a bridge for the upgrade, not a second support window: the fix is still the upgrade. PROCTOR check: mysql-eol.

    • For MySQL and MariaDB the check warns and does not fail yet. While Citadel's shared server runs 5.6, an app has no supported MySQL to move to there, so a security-only, Eol or EolGraceExpired version warns, and still says to move to 8.4 or later. It starts failing past the window when Citadel offers a supported MySQL (the stack's MySQL gate decision). PROCTOR check: mysql-eol (since PROCTOR 0.8.0).

    §5.4 Names, comments and connections

    • Table and column names SHOULD be descriptive. Add table and column comments (Laravel's ->comment()) where the database supports them, to say what an element is for (SHOULD) (WSU developer standards, 2024). No check exists yet.
    • The connection between the app and the database MUST be encrypted. The database account MUST have only the privileges the app needs, never an administrator account (WSU developer standards, 2024). No check exists yet.

    §5.5 Conventions that keep 5.6 working

    Each claim below about what 5.6 does names the probe that shows it on MySQL 5.6.51 (see "How the claims are proven", below).

    • An app MUST set Schema::defaultStringLength(191) in AppServiceProvider::boot(), before any migration runs. 5.6 caps an indexed utf8mb4 column at 767 bytes, which is 191 characters: an index on a 255 character string is refused (probe index-255) and one on 191 fits (probe index-191). PROCTOR check: mysql56.
    • An app MUST keep utf8mb4 and utf8mb4_unicode_ci, the defaults (probe collation-unicode), and MUST NOT use an 8.0-only collation such as utf8mb4_0900_ai_ci, which 5.6 does not know (probe collation-0900). No check exists yet.
    • An app MUST store JSON as text or longText, with Eloquent array or json casts, and MUST filter in PHP. 5.6 has no JSON column type (probe json-column) and no JSON functions (probe json-functions). PROCTOR check: mysql56.
    • An app MUST leave use_upsert_alias unset, so upsert() uses VALUES() (probe upsert-values). The row alias that setting switches to needs MySQL 8.0.19 (probe upsert-alias). PROCTOR check: mysql56.
    • An app MUST rename a column with raw DB::statement('ALTER TABLE ... CHANGE ...') (probe rename-column-change), and MUST NOT use renameColumn or renameIndex. On a 5.6 server Laravel 13's renameColumn first reads the column through the query 5.6 rejects (probe column-introspection), and on a newer one it writes RENAME COLUMN, which 5.6 cannot parse (probe rename-column-syntax); renameIndex writes RENAME INDEX, which arrived in 5.7 (probe rename-index). PROCTOR check: mysql56.
    • An app MUST use Schema::hasTable (probe has-table) and MUST NOT use column introspection: hasColumn, hasColumns, getColumns, getColumnListing and getColumnType. Laravel 13 reads them from information_schema.columns.generation_expression, a column 5.6 does not have, so the call fails outright (probe column-introspection). PROCTOR check: mysql56.
    • An app MUST skip db:show and db:monitor. PROCTOR check: mysql56.
    • An app SHOULD run one database-queue worker (or another driver if the platform offers one). 5.6 has no SKIP LOCKED (probe skip-locked), so a single worker avoids double-processing. No check exists yet.
    • An app MUST use timestamp, not date, for useCurrent() (probe timestamp-current-default). On a 5.6 server Laravel 13 drops useCurrent() from a date column without a word, so the migration passes, the column has no default, and an insert that leaves it out fails (probe use-current-date); 5.6 refuses a current-timestamp default on a date column in any case (probe date-current-default). PROCTOR check: mysql56.
    • An app MUST run migrations in CI against a real 5.6 container. SQLite-only tests pass code that 5.6 rejects. Held by: Preflight's mysql56-migrate component (0.6.0), which runs the migrations against MySQL 5.6.51 on an amd64 runner. PROCTOR check: mysql56-ci (0.15.0), which warns when an app with migrations has no such job.

    §5.6 Avoid until the server is upgraded

    §5.6.1 Schema

    • JSON and jsonb columns (probe json-column)
    • Generated columns, storedAs and virtualAs (probe generated-column)
    • renameIndex and renameColumn (probes rename-index, rename-column-syntax)
    • Column introspection (probe column-introspection)
    • invisible, instant and vector columns (probes invisible-column, vector-column; 8.4 has no vector type either)
    • InnoDB spatialIndex, which needs 5.7.5 (probe spatial-index-innodb)
    • DESC indexes and CHECK constraints. These are the quiet ones: 5.6 accepts both and then ignores them, so the migration passes, a DESC index is built ascending (probe desc-index-ignored) and a row that breaks a CHECK goes in (probe check-constraint-ignored). Validate in the app instead.

    §5.6.2 Queries

    • whereJson* and JSON-path updates (probe json-functions)
    • Window functions and CTEs (probes window-function, cte)
    • SKIP LOCKED and NOWAIT in raw SQL (probes skip-locked, nowait)
    • joinLateral (probe join-lateral)
    • Joined deletes with an order or a limit (probe joined-delete-order-limit; no MySQL release accepts these, so they stay out after the upgrade too)

    §5.6.3 Commands

    • db:show
    • db:monitor

    §5.7 Moving to 8.4

    Code that follows the conventions and avoids the patterns above runs unchanged on 8.4: every probe statement 5.6.51 accepts, 8.4.13 accepts too, except a row that breaks a CHECK constraint, which the list above already avoids. What the move changes, each shown on 8.4.13 by the same probe:

    • The patterns above start working: JSON columns and functions, generated and invisible columns, InnoDB spatial indexes, the upsert row alias, column introspection, renameColumn and renameIndex, CTEs, window functions, SKIP LOCKED, NOWAIT and joinLateral. Two stay out: vector columns and joined deletes with an order or a limit.
    • The two quiet ones turn real. 8.4 builds a DESC index descending (probe desc-index-ignored) and enforces a CHECK constraint, refusing the row 5.6 let in (probe check-constraint-ignored). A CHECK written while an app was on 5.6 has never refused anything, so test the code that writes to that table before the move.
    • useCurrent() on a date column gets its default back: from 8.0.13 Laravel 13 writes default (CURDATE()), which 8.4 accepts and 5.6 cannot parse (probe date-current-expression). A plain current-timestamp default on a date column is still refused (probe date-current-default), and the timestamp convention keeps working.
    • Large prefixes are always on. innodb_large_prefix no longer exists (probe large-prefix-off), ROW_FORMAT=DYNAMIC is honored without a warning (probe row-format-dynamic), and a 255 character utf8mb4 index fits (probes index-255, row-format-dynamic-index). defaultStringLength(191) does no harm there, so it can stay until the app leaves 5.6 for good.

    On 5.6 itself, the server-side large-prefix settings (innodb_large_prefix=ON, innodb_file_format=Barracuda, DYNAMIC rows) are a question for the database owners, not something an app sets: a stock 5.6.51 has large prefixes off (probe large-prefix-off). Passing ROW_FORMAT=DYNAMIC through the connection's engine setting does not get around that: on the default Antelope file format 5.6 warns and builds a COMPACT table (probe row-format-dynamic), and the 255 character index is still refused (probe row-format-dynamic-index). defaultStringLength(191) is the convention that works.

    Oracle moved 5.6 to Sustaining Support on 2021-02-01, so it gets no new fixes. Builds older than 5.6.46 also speak only TLS 1.0 (MySQL 5.6.46 added TLS 1.1 and 1.2, per its release notes), which current hosts may refuse. The probes cannot show this one: the stock 5.6.51 image starts with TLS off. Both are reasons to plan the move rather than wait for it.

    §5.8 How the stack checks it

    PROCTOR's mysql56 check warns on the patterns the shared 5.6 server rejects: JSON columns and queries, generated columns, renameColumn and renameIndex, vector, invisible and spatial columns, column introspection, the raw-SQL syntax, the upsert row alias, indexed strings over 191 characters, a missing Schema::defaultStringLength(191), date columns defaulting to the current time, and the db:show and db:monitor commands. It warns rather than fails: an app on its own newer database is not affected.

    §5.9 How the claims are proven

    Every "probe" named in this chapter is one statement in CREED's tools/Mysql56/Probes.php: the SQL Laravel 13 sends (read from its MySQL grammars at 13.40.0), or the raw statement this chapter tells an app to write instead, with the answer 5.6 gives. php bin/mysql56-probe.php runs them against a live server, in the session Laravel 13 opens (utf8mb4_unicode_ci, its strict sql_mode), and prints [OK] or [FAIL] per probe. scripts/mysql56-probe.sh (Linux, macOS) and scripts/mysql56-probe.ps1 (Windows) start mysql:5.6.51, the image Squire runs and Preflight's mysql56-migrate component tests against, and run them. CREED's own pipeline runs them on that component, on every main and tag pipeline. All 32 agreed with this chapter on 2026-11-11.

    Each probe also records the answer MySQL 8.4.13 gives, which is where "Moving to 8.4" comes from. scripts/mysql56-probe.sh 8.4 (or scripts/mysql56-probe.ps1 -Server 8.4) and the pipeline's mysql84-probe job run the same probes on mysql:8.4.13 and judge each against that answer. On 2026-11-11 all 32 agreed with their 8.4 answers, and 22 of those answers differ from 5.6's, which is the point: the patterns above are 5.6 limits, and the upgrade lifts most of them.

    The probes read stock images. The shared server keeps its own settings, which its owners know; a probe that says "the default" means the image's.
